Maintenance Report — MNT-0039-014

Asset: WELL-0039 (SW-23 Well 039, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 13 Dec 2024 08:00 · Finished: 14 Dec 2024 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 18 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0039-0108 on 2024-12-12 Report written: 15 Dec 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0039-0108 at 14:00 on 2024-12-12 found crude oil on the pad: about 6.7% of the pad area, estimated 2.7 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 276 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 221 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.3 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0039-014 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.23% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0039-024

Asset: WELL-0039 (SW-23 Well 039, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 28 Jun 2026 08:00 · Finished: 22 Jul 2026 16:00 · Well stopped for this job: 584 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0039-0188 on 2026-06-25 Report written: 22 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0039-0188 showed the wellhead at 39.3 °C with the air at 38.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 276 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 221 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0039-024 (WS-06).
